You are fixing a bug in the Go repository checked out at /echo (module github.com/labstack/echo/v4, the Echo web framework). Work only inside /echo. Do not use the internet. Do not edit any *_test.go file (pre-existing tests must not be modified).

BUG: In /echo/middleware/proxy.go the Proxy middleware panics when the configured ProxyBalancer has no targets. `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` index into `b.targets` unconditionally (e.g. `b.targets[b.random.Intn(len(b.targets))]`, `b.i = b.i % uint32(len(b.targets))`), so with zero targets they panic with 'index out of range' / 'integer divide by zero'. The middleware handler in ProxyWithConfig also uses the returned target without a nil check.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR (this is the contract you must implement): a hidden test named `TestProxyBalancerWithNoTargets` in package `middleware` (not present in the repo) will create `NewRandomBalancer(nil)` and `NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)`, wire them into `Proxy(...)`, serve a request, and expect the response status to be `http.StatusServiceUnavailable` (503) with no panic. So:
  1. In `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` (and any equivalent code in middleware/proxy_1_11.go / middleware/proxy_1_11_n.go, which are build-tag variants of the same balancers), return `nil` when `len(b.targets) == 0`.
  2. In `ProxyWithConfig`'s returned handler, right after `tgt := config.Balancer.Next(c)`, add `if tgt == nil { return echo.ErrServiceUnavailable }` (before `c.Set(config.ContextKey, tgt)`).
Keep the change minimal and idiomatic; do not refactor unrelated code, do not add new features, do not change other files.

TASKS:
1. First run `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and record which tests already fail BEFORE your edit (these are the only ones allowed to fail afterwards).
2. Apply the fix.
3. Verify: `cd /echo && gofmt -l middleware/ && go build ./... && go vet ./middleware/ && go test ./middleware/ -run 'TestProxy' -v 2>&1 | tail -40` and then the full `go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. Also write a temporary throwaway test OUTSIDE the repo test files (e.g. in /tmp as a separate module is hard; instead you may temporarily create /echo/middleware/zz_tmp_nil_target_test.go, run it, and DELETE it afterwards) that asserts both balancers return 503 for a request when they have no targets, plus that `Next` returns nil. Confirm the temporary file is deleted at the end (`ls /echo/middleware`).

REPORT BACK: the exact diff (git diff), the before/after test results, confirmation that no pre-existing test newly fails, and confirmation that the temporary test file was removed.

Independently verify a fix in the Go repo at /echo (module github.com/labstack/echo/v4). Do NOT edit any file except as described in step 3 (a temporary test you must delete afterwards). Do not use the internet.

A fix was just applied to /echo/middleware/proxy.go so that proxy balancers with no targets return nil from `Next` and `ProxyWithConfig`'s handler returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) instead of panicking.

Do this:
1. `cd /echo && git status --porcelain && git diff` — confirm the only modified file is middleware/proxy.go, no untracked leftover files, and no *_test.go file is modified.
2. `cd /echo && go build ./... && go vet ./middleware/ && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -20` — confirm everything passes.
3. Write a temporary test /echo/middleware/zz_verify_tmp_test.go (package middleware) that, for both `NewRandomBalancer(nil)` and `NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)`: asserts `b.Next(nil) == nil`, and serves a request through `echo.New()` + `e.Use(Proxy(b))` + `e.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil))` asserting `rec.Code == http.StatusServiceUnavailable` (503) and that nothing panics. Run `go test ./middleware/ -run TestZZVerifyTmp -v`. Then DELETE the temporary file and confirm with `ls /echo/middleware | grep -i zz` (no output) and `git status --porcelain` (only middleware/proxy.go modified).

REPORT BACK: raw command outputs for each step, whether the verification passed, and confirmation that no temporary file remains.

BUG REPORT (from the user): There is a bug in `/echo/context.go`. Once fixed, these hidden tests in package `echo` (NOT present in the repo; their names describe the expected behaviour) should pass:
  - `TestContext_Scheme`
  - `TestContext_Scheme/ignores_invalid_X-Forwarded-Proto_and_uses_X-Forwarded-Protocol`
  - `TestContext_Scheme/ignores_invalid_forwarded_headers_and_falls_back_to_http`

YOUR JOB:
1. Read the `Scheme()` method on `echo.Context` in /echo/context.go (and any helpers it uses, e.g. in /echo/echo.go, /echo/ip.go, and the existing `TestContext_Scheme` in /echo/context_test.go for the currently-tested behaviour). Work out the genuine repository-evident bug: `Scheme()` should read the scheme from the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header, and when that value is not a valid scheme it must be ignored and the next fallback used — specifically the `X-Forwarded-Protocol` header — and if that is also invalid/absent it must fall back to `http` (or `https` when the request is TLS / `X-Forwarded-Ssl: on`). Use the code's own comments/docstrings and the existing test cases as the contract. Typical real bug: the header value is not validated (e.g. `strings.ToLower` comparison against "https"/"http" vs a proper `url.Parse`-based validity check) so an invalid value such as `"invalid"` or `"ftp"` is returned as-is instead of being ignored, or the `X-Forwarded-Protocol` fallback is missing/never reached.
2. Fix the bug minimally and idiomatically in context.go (only there unless the root cause is clearly elsewhere — explain if so). Do not add features, do not refactor unrelated code.
3. Verify: first record BEFORE results with `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` (ideally all green, so afterwards nothing may fail), then after the edit run `gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`.
4. Write a temporary test /echo/zz_tmp_scheme_test.go (package echo) reproducing the three hidden scenarios: (a) plain request -> http, TLS request -> https, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` -> https; (b) `X-Forwarded-Proto: invalid` plus `X-Forwarded-Protocol: https` -> https; (c) `X-Forwarded-Proto: invalid` and no other headers -> http. Run it, then DELETE it and confirm with `ls /echo | grep -i zz` (no output) and `git status --porcelain`.

REPORT BACK: the exact `git diff`, the before/after test results, your reasoning about the bug, and confirmation that no pre-existing test newly fails and no temporary file remains.
